deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (inferred, not stated on the page): this is an observation log for calibrating the graduation (division) errors of a divided circle on an astronomical instrument. The words 'Kreis in Ost' mean 'circle in the East position', which is the language of a meridian circle (Göttingen had instruments by Reichenbach and Repsold). The circle is read by several microscopes. The header gives their placement: I at z, II at z+270°, III at z+90°, and a microscope '0' at z+315°. The next page's margin seems to read '0 z+45'; since 315° = −45°, this is consistent. The setting z is stepped through 0°, 15°, …, 345° (24 settings).

TOP LINES: these are the constant mean offsets of the microscopes, i.e. the departure of their spacing from the nominal 270° and 90°.
- 24 Sept: II−I = −5′18.2″ and III−I = −1′51.4″.
- 28 Oct: −5′18.9″ and −1′52.65″.
- The note 'Oct. 25 eben so' means 25 Oct gave the same values.
- So the microscope constants agree between sessions to 0.7″ and 1.25″.

LEFT TABLE (24 Sept): residual readings in arc-seconds for microscopes I, II, III at each z. They appear to be referred to the microscope at z+315 and freed of the constant offsets above.
- My check: the column sums are −0.4, −0.7 and +1.75, so the means are about 0. This is consistent with means having been removed. The '−0.4' written at the head of the previous page may be this sum for column I.
- The three columns are strongly correlated. This means the dominant signal is a function of the circle position z common to all microscopes, i.e. it is the graduation error, not microscope noise.

MIDDLE: the heading reads 'c′z + c″(z+45°) wird dargestellt durch' ('… is represented by'), followed by a series. Here c′ and c″ presumably denote the corrections of the graduation at the two places read. The series is:
−0.05″ + 3.37 cos 2(·) + 0.13 cos 4(·) − 0.23 cos 6(·) + 1.81 cos 8(·) − 0.53 cos 10(·) + 0.15 cos 12(·).
- Only even cosine harmonics appear. That would follow if the represented quantity is even in its argument and has period 180°, which is what folding a 24-point set by symmetry produces.
- Which argument, and which combination of the tabulated columns, is meant is not stated. Evaluated at argument 0, the series gives 4.65. That does not equal any single tabulated value at z=0 (3.0, 1.4, 1.2) or their mean.
- So the exact referent cannot be confirmed from this page. It is presumably a derived combination worked out elsewhere.
- The next page carries out a full 24-ordinate harmonic analysis of column I ('Darstellung von I für Kreis in Ost'). It uses the folding scheme (α, β, γ, δ = α−γ, ε = 2β; logarithms) and yields coefficients of cos 1…12 and sin 1…11.

RIGHT TABLE (28 Oct, same circle position): a repeat of the whole series of 24 settings × 3 microscopes.
- It reproduces the September pattern to within about 1–2″, e.g. z=210: 7.7/6.7/8.0 versus 6.2/6.3/7.3.
- So the observed periodic pattern is a real instrumental (division) error.

OVERALL: the page records repeated observations of circle-division errors and represents them by a trigonometric (Fourier) series, as the input to harmonic analysis.
errors: No demonstrable arithmetic errors can be established: the page is primarily raw observation data.

The cosine series (−0.05 + 3.37cos2 + … + 0.15cos12) cannot be verified against the tables on this page. Its value at argument 0 (4.65) does not match any tabulated z=0 entry, so its referent (which combination, which argument scaling) is unclear. This is not a provable error.
Column sums of the Sept table (−0.4, −0.7, +1.75) are not exactly zero. This is consistent with rounding of separately reduced readings, not a slip.

results.what: Determination of graduation (division) errors of a meridian-circle limb by reading several microscopes at fixed angular separations over 24 equidistant settings, with session-to-session repetition.
results.modern_name: Calibration of circle graduation errors (Bessel/Hansen-type method of diameters/microscope combinations)
results.usually_credited_to: Bessel (1820s, Königsberg); later Hansen and others developed systematic schemes

results.what: Representation of the periodic error as a truncated trigonometric series with only even cosine terms up to the 12th harmonic (24-point data).
results.modern_name: Discrete Fourier / harmonic analysis (trigonometric interpolation with 24 ordinates)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Theoria interpolationis, c.1805, publ. 1866), Bessel; FFT-like folding later credited to Cooley–Tukey 1965 but traced to Gauss by Heideman–Johnson–Burrus 1984

results.what: Microscope constant offsets II−I and III−I with their stability across sessions (≈0.7″ and 1.25″ change).

deep.surprise_reason: These are observational calibration data with a Fourier representation. Gauss's harmonic analysis and his work with the Göttingen meridian circles are well documented, and nothing here goes beyond known practice.

checkable.asserts: Sum of Sept column I is -0.4 (mean ≈ 0).
Sum of Sept column II is -0.7.
Sum of Sept column III is +1.75.
Value of the written cosine series at argument 0 is 4.65.
Change of II−I offset between Sept 24 and Oct 28 is -0.7 arcsec.
Change of III−I offset is -1.25 arcsec.

transcription_corrections: Header placements read 'I z, II z+270, III z+90, 0 z+315'. The '2' in the previous-page transcription is z.
The right-edge table on the previous page's transcription is this page (the Sept 24 table), not a separate dataset.
Right table, z=135, column I: possibly '−1,0' rather than '−0,0'.
Right table, z=225 III ('+5.6') and z=240 III ('+0.0') are overwritten or blotted. The readings are uncertain.
Right table, z=300, column II '−3.9' has an ink blot over the sign.
